name: TFmini Plus LiDAR distance sensor
description: Benewake single-point time-of-flight LiDAR in an IP65 enclosure, measuring 0.1-12 m (+/-5 cm up to 6 m, +/-1% beyond) at 100 frames/s (1-1000 Hz adjustable), streaming 9-byte frames (distance in cm, signal strength, chip temperature) over a 115200-baud 3.3 V UART. Needs 5 V +/-0.5 V, about 110 mA average and 500 mA peak. Sold as: SparkFun TFMini Plus - Micro LiDAR Module (SEN-15179), the Benewake module with its 30 cm GH1.25-4P cable: +5V (red), RXD (white), TXD (blue), GND (black).
eli5: Shines an invisible infrared light beam and times how long it takes to bounce back, so your board knows how far away the wall or object in front of it is, up to 12 metres. Its case keeps out dust and splashes.

pins.name: +5V
pins.description: Supply, 5 V +/-0.5 V (pin 1, red wire); draws up to 500 mA peak, so feed it from a 5 V supply that can give at least 500 mA

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Sensor serial input, 3.3 V LVTTL (pin 2, white wire): wire to the board's UART TX; only needed to send commands

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Sensor serial output, 3.3 V LVTTL, 115200 baud (pin 3, blue wire): wire to the board's UART RX

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (pin 4, black wire); join it to the microcontroller's GND

buildNotes: Power from a 5 V supply (4.5-5.5 V) that can deliver the 500 mA peak current the manual asks for; join its GND to the microcontroller's GND. A board's USB 5V pin may brown out on the peaks, so use a separate 5 V supply.
The data wires are 3.3 V logic: safe straight into an ESP32 or Pico. Cross them: sensor TXD (blue) -> board RX, sensor RXD (white) -> board TX (only needed to send commands).
The cable order differs from the TFmini-S: pin 1 red +5V, pin 2 white RXD, pin 3 blue TXD, pin 4 black GND.

115200 baud 8N1. The sensor streams 100 frames a second by itself: 0x59 0x59, distance (cm, low byte first), strength, temperature, then a checksum = low 8 bits of the sum of the first 8 bytes. Resync on 0x59 0x59 and drop frames with a bad checksum.
Flush the UART before each reading: frames pile up 900 bytes a second, so a program that reads slowly otherwise gets old distances.
Distance 0 means the reading is unreliable (signal strength under 100 or 65535: target too far, too dark or absent). Readings under 10 cm (the blind zone) are unreliable.
Glass, water and mirror-like surfaces give wrong distances. After changing any setting send 'save settings' (5A 04 11 6F) or it does not take effect.
The GH1.25 cable does not plug into a breadboard: use a GH1.25-to-Dupont lead or solder the wires to a 4-pin header.

driver.code:
# Benewake TFmini Plus LiDAR distance sensor (UART mode), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Benewake "SJ-PM-TFmini Plus-T-01 A01 Product Manual" and the
# "SJ-GU-TFmini-Plus-01 A02" datasheet:
# UART 115200 baud, 8N1 (Table 5). In the default standard format the sensor sends a 9-byte frame
# by itself at the frame rate (100 Hz by default):
#   0x59 0x59 Dist_L Dist_H Strength_L Strength_H Temp_L Temp_H Checksum
#   checksum = low 8 bits of the sum of the first 8 bytes.
# Dist is in cm by default (0-1200), or mm after the "output format 06" command.
# When the signal strength is below 100 or equal to 65535 the reading is unreliable and the
# sensor sets Dist to 0 (manual 5.3). Chip temperature in C = Temp / 8 - 256.
# Host commands (Table 7/8): 0x5A, total length, ID, little-endian payload, then the low 8 bits
# of the sum of all previous bytes. Send "save settings" after changing anything.
import time

_HEAD = 0x59
_FRAME_LEN = 9


def _command(cmd_id, payload=b''):
    body = bytes((0x5A, len(payload) + 4, cmd_id)) + bytes(payload)
    return body + bytes((sum(body) & 0xFF,))


class TFminiPlus:
    def __init__(self, uart):
        """uart: a machine.UART at 115200 baud whose RX is wired to the sensor's TXD (blue wire)."""
        self.uart = uart
        self._buf = b''
        self.unit = 'cm'
        self.error = None

    def flush(self):
        """Throw away buffered (stale) bytes so the next read returns a fresh frame."""
        n = self.uart.any()
        while n:
            self.uart.read(n)
            n = self.uart.any()
        self._buf = b''

    def _frame(self, timeout_ms):
        deadline = time.ticks_add(time.ticks_ms(), timeout_ms)
        while True:
            # resync on 0x59 0x59 and check every candidate frame's checksum
            while len(self._buf) >= 2:
                if self._buf[0] != _HEAD or self._buf[1] != _HEAD:
                    self._buf = self._buf[1:]
                    continue
                if len(self._buf) < _FRAME_LEN:
                    break
                f = self._buf[:_FRAME_LEN]
                if sum(f[:8]) & 0xFF == f[8]:
                    self._buf = self._buf[_FRAME_LEN:]
                    return f
                self._buf = self._buf[1:]  # corrupted or false header: resync
            if time.ticks_diff(deadline, time.ticks_ms()) <= 0:
                raise OSError('TFmini Plus: no valid frame (check TXD -> board RX, 5 V supply, 115200 baud)')
            n = self.uart.any()
            if n:
                got = self.uart.read(n)
                if got:
                    self._buf += got
            else:
                time.sleep_ms(2)

    def read(self, timeout_ms=500, fresh=True):
        """Return (distance, strength, temperature_c) from the next valid frame.
        distance is in self.unit ('cm' by default) and is None when the sensor flags the reading as
        unreliable (it sends 0 when strength < 100 or = 65535); self.error then says why.
        fresh=True drops bytes that piled up while the program was busy elsewhere."""
        if fresh:
            self.flush()
        f = self._frame(timeout_ms)
        dist = f[2] | (f[3] << 8)
        strength = f[4] | (f[5] << 8)
        temp_c = (f[6] | (f[7] << 8)) / 8 - 256
        self.error = None
        if dist == 0 or strength < 100 or strength == 65535:
            self.error = 'unreliable (signal strength %d)' % strength
            dist = None
        return dist, strength, temp_c

    def distance(self, timeout_ms=500):
        """Distance in self.unit, or None if unreliable."""
        return self.read(timeout_ms)[0]

    # ---- configuration commands (Table 8); need the sensor's RXD (white wire) on the UART TX ----
    def _send(self, cmd_id, payload=b'', reply_len=0, timeout_ms=200):
        self.flush()
        self.uart.write(_command(cmd_id, payload))
        if not reply_len:
            return None
        deadline = time.ticks_add(time.ticks_ms(), timeout_ms)
        buf = b''
        while time.ticks_diff(deadline, time.ticks_ms()) > 0:
            n = self.uart.any()
            if n:
                buf += self.uart.read(n) or b''
                i = buf.find(bytes((0x5A, reply_len, cmd_id)))
                if i >= 0 and len(buf) >= i + reply_len:
                    r = buf[i:i + reply_len]
                    if sum(r[:-1]) & 0xFF == r[-1]:
                        return r
            else:
                time.sleep_ms(2)
        return None

    def version(self):
        """Firmware version as (major, minor, revision), or None. Reply 5A 07 01 V1 V2 V3 SU = V3.V2.V1."""
        r = self._send(0x01, b'', 7)
        return (r[5], r[4], r[3]) if r else None

    def set_frame_rate(self, hz):
        """Frame rate in Hz: 0 (triggered with trigger()) or 1000/n for a whole n, 1-1000. Call save() after."""
        return self._send(0x03, bytes((hz & 0xFF, hz >> 8)), 6) is not None

    def trigger(self):
        """With frame rate 0: ask for one measurement; then call read(fresh=False)."""
        self.flush()
        self.uart.write(_command(0x04))

    def set_unit_mm(self, mm=True):
        """Standard 9-byte output in mm (True) or cm (False). Call save() after."""
        ok = self._send(0x05, bytes((0x06 if mm else 0x01,)), 5) is not None
        if ok:
            self.unit = 'mm' if mm else 'cm'
        return ok

    def output(self, enable):
        """Enable or disable the frame stream."""
        return self._send(0x07, bytes((1 if enable else 0,)), 5) is not None

    def save(self):
        """Store settings in flash."""
        r = self._send(0x11, b'', 5, 1000)
        return bool(r) and r[3] == 0

    def reset(self):
        """System reset (wait about 1 s afterwards)."""
        r = self._send(0x02, b'', 5, 1000)
        time.sleep_ms(1000)
        return bool(r) and r[3] == 0

    def factory_reset(self):
        r = self._send(0x10, b'', 5, 1000)
        return bool(r) and r[3] == 0

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from tfmini_plus import TFminiPlus

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=115200, tx=Pin({RXD}), rx=Pin({TXD}))
lidar = TFminiPlus(uart)
while True:
    d, s, t = lidar.read()
    if d is None:
        print('no reading:', lidar.error)
    else:
        print('D=%dcm S=%d T=%.1fC' % (d, s, t))
    time.sleep_ms(500)
